title: Choose the visual world for SYSTEM // SELF
question: The roll assigned the System Window. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: System Window
options.thesis: A quiet native app where everything THE SYSTEM says arrives as a bracketed System window.
options.viewport: Today: a System window with the morning briefing, the rank as one giant letter, five domain bands, quests below, labeled nav bar.
options.risk: Closest to the near-black-plus-neon AI default and to fan-art costume; it must stay flat, no glow.

raised.raise: Three type sizes only, on a strict measure, instead of 23.
Domain colour owns whole bands, not 2px bars.
Everything sits on one visible 8dp cell grid and reflows by whole cells.
One giant figure per screen: the rank letter carries the hierarchy.

options.label: Rank Card
options.thesis: Your life as an official result card: rank, percentile, five subject scores, a stamped remark.
options.viewport: Today: a result-card header with the rank huge, a ruled score table of five domains with change columns, the remark stamped, quests as numbered rows.
options.risk: A light, official look at night, and an exam artifact some users find stressful; also the most familiar idea for this audience.

options.label: One Thing At A Time
options.thesis: Today is a vertical stack of full-screen cards: the briefing, then each quest, each drenched in its domain colour.
options.viewport: A full-screen BODY-red quest card, title low-left, reward and deadline, Complete / Briefing / Refuse stacked on a right rail.
options.case: This audience lives in Reels, so it wins on recognition, but stats, rivals and history need a second, denser surface.
options.risk: Dense screens (stats, finance) can't use the feed and may feel like a different app.

options.label: Quest Coupons
options.thesis: Quests are coupons: valid until done, then stamped USED or VOID; nothing disappears, it cancels.
options.viewport: A coupon book: today's quests as tear-off coupons with domain, reward and deadline boxes, one stamped VOID.
options.case: Very clear quest states and matches 'every entry is permanent', but the audience doesn't identify with airline paper.
options.risk: Light theme and a retro carrier look that can read as a travel app.

options.label: Lexicon Page
options.thesis: Entries ranked by apparatus on a fixed measure.
options.viewport: A column of entries with guide words.
options.case: Loses both axes: the audience doesn't read lexicons, and it hides the game.
options.risk: Bookish costume on a phone app.

options.label: Guide Map
options.thesis: Areas as swelling lobes of flat colour.
options.viewport: One domain lobe filling the screen.
options.case: Loses both axes: playful and warm where the product is cold.

options.label: Grid Specimen
options.thesis: Letterforms built on a visible grid.
options.viewport: A rank letter built from grid cells.
options.case: Loses both axes: design-school, not anime or gaming.
options.kept: One cell grid that everything reflows on.

options.label: Type Specimen
options.thesis: Weight that morphs with a slider.
options.viewport: One giant glyph and a readout.
options.case: Loses both axes, though 'score drives weight' was tempting.
options.risk: A font demo, not a life OS.
options.kept: Hierarchy by scale contrast: one giant figure per screen.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean Material 3 dark habit/fitness tracker, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Greeting, progress rings for the five domains, a checklist of quests, a labeled nav bar.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every habit tracker by design.
